title: Grothendieck spectral sequence and its Leray specialization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories,
$\mathcal C$ an abelian category, and $\Phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$,
$\Psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ additive left exact functors forming a
composable pair with acyclicity in the sense of [det-def-groth-ss]
($\Phi$ sends injective objects to $\Psi$-acyclic objects). Then for
every $A\in\mathcal A$ there is a first-quadrant cohomological spectral
sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}\cong R^p\Psi\bigl(R^q\Phi(A)\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ R^{p+q}(\Psi\circ\Phi)(A).
$$

In particular, let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be morphisms of sites (or
schemes with their étale or small Zariski sites). For an abelian
sheaf $F$ on $X$, since $f_*$ carries injectives
to $h_*$-acyclics ($f_*$ is right adjoint to the exact $f^{-1}$, so
it preserves injectives), there is a spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^ph_*R^qf_*F\ \Longrightarrow\ R^{p+q}(hf)_*F.
$$

For $Z$ the punctual site, so that $h_*=\Gamma(Y,-)$, this is the
*Leray* spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Y,R^qf_*F)\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}(X,F).
$$

In particular this includes $Y_{\mathrm{zar}}$ and $X_{\mathrm{zar}}$
for a morphism of schemes. For proper $f$ and coherent $F$ the
Zariski sequence is the spectral sequence of
$\Gamma(Y,-)\circ f_*$ on $\cO$-modules.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $A\to I^\bullet$ concentrated in nonnegative degrees, using enough injectives in $\mathcal A$. To construct the resolution, embed $Q^0=A$ in an injective $I^0$, set $Q^{n+1}=\operatorname{coker}(Q^n\hookrightarrow I^n)$, embed $Q^{n+1}$ in $I^{n+1}$, and use the composite $I^n\twoheadrightarrow Q^{n+1}\hookrightarrow I^{n+1}$ as differential. Its image equals the next kernel, which gives exactness. Set $K^a=\Phi(I^a)$, so $H^b(K)=R^b\Phi(A)$. The category $\mathcal B$ also has enough injectives, so choose the first-quadrant Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $K^\bullet\to J^{a,b}$ supplied by the cited existence lemma. Its columns resolve $K^a$; its horizontal cycles, boundaries and cohomology in each fixed resolution degree are injective, and their vertical complexes resolve the corresponding cycles, boundaries and cohomology of $K$. Put $D^{a,b}=\Psi(J^{a,b})$. Additivity makes this a first-quadrant double complex in the abelian category $\mathcal C$. No injectives in $\mathcal C$ are needed.

Apply the double-complex spectral-sequence theorem to $D$. For the filtration by the original complex degree, ${}'E_1^{a,b}=H^b(\Psi(J^{a,\bullet}))=R^b\Psi(K^a)$, by computation on the chosen column resolution. The acyclicity assumption says this is zero for $b>0$; for $b=0$ it is $\Psi(K^a)$. The $d_1$ differential is induced by the differential of $K$, by the augmented column maps and the natural $R^0\Psi\cong\Psi$ identification. Thus ${}'E_2^{a,0}=H^a(\Psi(K^\bullet))$ and all other rows vanish. The row-collapse lemma identifies $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ with $H^n(\Psi\Phi(I^\bullet))=R^n(\Psi\circ\Phi)(A)$. The last equality uses the original injective resolution and the definition and well-definedness of right derived functors; the composite is additive left exact because both functors preserve kernels and finite biproducts.

For the other filtration the filtration index is the resolution degree: its first page is ${}''E_1^{b,a}=H^a(\Psi(J^{\bullet,b}))$. Apply the left-exact cohomology comparison to each horizontal row: its cycles and boundaries are injective by the Cartan--Eilenberg statement, so this is canonically $\Psi(H^a(J^{\bullet,b}))$. The vertical complex $H^a(J^{\bullet,\bullet})$ is an injective resolution of $H^a(K)$, hence ${}''E_2^{b,a}=R^b\Psi(H^a(K))=R^b\Psi(R^a\Phi(A))$. The comparisons commute with the unsigned vertical differential, since they are induced by cycle inclusions and quotient maps. With the total differential $d_I+(-1)^a d_{II}$ of [def-sp-double-complex-total], the second first-page differential on the row of fixed horizontal cohomological degree $a$ is $(-1)^a\Psi(d_{II})$. Its cochain complex is isomorphic to the unsigned one by multiplication by $(-1)^{ab}$ in resolution degree $b$: $(-1)^{a(b+1)}(-1)^a=(-1)^{ab}$. This elementary sign correction gives the stated second page. Rename the indices $(b,a)=(p,q)$. The double-complex theorem supplies convergence to $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ and its finite image filtration; transfer that filtration through the isomorphism of step 2. This gives exactly the displayed abutment in the sense of [det-def-groth-ss].

For the site specialization use the categories of abelian sheaves on the sites $X,Y,Z$. They are abelian with enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Steps 1--3 used Grothendieckness of the source and intermediate categories only to obtain enough injectives, and used the acyclicity hypothesis only as $R^q\Psi(\Phi(I))=0$ for $q>0$, so they apply verbatim. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3) a morphism of sites $f:X\to Y$ is given by a continuous functor $u$, with $f_*\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u$ and $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. For sheaf morphisms $a,b$ we have $(f_*(a+b))_V=a_{u(V)}+b_{u(V)}$, so $f_*$ is additive. Kernels and finite products of abelian sheaves are sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and precomposition preserves them, so $f_*$ is left exact, and likewise $h_*$. Since $f^{-1}$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $f_*$ preserves injectives [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], and an injective is $h_*$-acyclic [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. Apply steps 1--3 to $(f_*,h_*)$. If $h$ is given by $v$, the composite $hf$ is given by $u\circ v$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] $(hf)_*=h_*f_*$ on objects and morphisms, so the abutment is $R^{p+q}(hf)_*F$. Let $Z$ be the punctual site (one object $*$, the identity covering). Then $h_*\mathcal G=\mathcal G(v(*))=\Gamma(v(*),\mathcal G)$, which is what the statement calls $\Gamma(Y,-)$. Likewise $(hf)_*=\Gamma(u(v(*)),-)$ is $\Gamma(X,-)$. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2), $R^p\Gamma(U,-)=H^p(U,-)$, and the Leray formula follows.

Now let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$ be morphisms of schemes, with their small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] or small Zariski sites [def-sc-zariski-site]. *Etale sites.* By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact], base change $V\mapsto V\times_YX$ defines a morphism of sites $X_{\Et}\to Y_{\Et}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), with $f_*F(V)=F(V\times_YX)$. The same holds for $h$ and $hf$, so step 4 applies. The composite of [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] is $W\mapsto(W\times_ZY)\times_YX$. The canonical isomorphisms $(W\times_ZY)\times_YX\cong W\times_ZX$, natural in $W$, identify it with base change along $hf$. Hence $(hf)_*\cong h_*f_*$. Isomorphic left exact functors have isomorphic derived functors: apply the isomorphism termwise to one injective resolution [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. *Zariski sites.* An abelian sheaf on $X_{\rm Zar}$ is an abelian sheaf on the underlying space of $X$, and $f_*F(V)=F(f^{-1}V)$. By [lem-sc-topological-pushforward-injective], $f^{-1}$ is exact and left adjoint to $f_*$, and $f_*$ preserves injectives. The other inputs of step 4 (enough injectives, sectionwise left exactness, acyclicity of injectives) hold as there, and $(hf)_*=h_*f_*$ exactly since $(hf)^{-1}W=f^{-1}h^{-1}W$. *Leray for schemes.* On both sites $Y$ (resp. $\mathrm{id}_Y$) is a final object. $\Gamma(Y,-)$ is evaluation there, which is additive and left exact with $H^p(Y,-)=R^p\Gamma(Y,-)$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2). Also $\Gamma(Y,f_*F)=F(X)=\Gamma(X,F)$ on objects and morphisms, since $Y\times_YX=X$ and $f^{-1}Y=X$. Because $f_*$ preserves injectives, steps 1--3 applied to $(f_*,\Gamma(Y,-))$ give $H^p(Y,R^qf_*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$.

proof.text: For the Zariski module case, take $\Phi=f_*:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $\Psi=\Gamma(Y,-)$, with values in modules over $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$. The two sheaf-module categories are abelian with enough injectives. Both functors are additive and left exact: for $f_*$ the sections over $V$ are those over $f^{-1}V$ with scalars restricted through $f^\sharp$, and kernels are sectionwise; for $\Gamma$ evaluate those kernels at $Y$. The cited module pushforward acyclicity statement, with $V=Y$, gives that $f_*I$ is $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic for every injective module $I$. Apply the construction in steps 1--3, which needs only enough injectives, not exactness of the module pullback. Since $(f_*F)(Y)=F(X)$ also on morphisms, the composite is global sections on $X$, with scalars restricted from $\mathcal O_X(X)$ to $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$. Its derived functors are therefore $H^n(X,F)$, with that scalar restriction (kernels, images and quotient groups are unchanged on restricting scalars), and $R^p\Psi(R^q\Phi F)=H^p(Y,R^qf_*F)$. This proves the module Leray sequence for every module sheaf, hence for the proper coherent case in the statement; properness and coherence impose no additional requirement on this construction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_leraySpectralSequence [HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]
    [HasInjectiveResolutions Y.Modules] (ℱ : X.Modules) :
    ∃ E : E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequenceNat AddCommGrpCat.{u},
      (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty ((E.page 2).X (p, q) ≅
        ((globalSectionsFunctor Y).rightDerived p).obj ((higherDirectImage f q).obj ℱ))) ∧
      E.AbutsTo (fun n ↦ ((globalSectionsFunctor X).rightDerived n).obj ℱ)
lean.note: Existing attachment to exactly the three declarations named by the current blueprint. The abstract Functor.exists_grothendieckSpectralSequence theorem and Adjunction.isAcyclicComposablePair are defined in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.Grothendieck, publicly imported by the recorded module; Scheme.Modules.exists_leraySpectralSequence is defined in the recorded module. The abstract theorem gives the full abstract statement with an arbitrary abelian target, the adjunction theorem supplies acyclicity for direct images of abelian sheaves on sites via their exact inverse-image adjoints, and the primary module theorem gives the Zariski module Leray specialization (hence its proper coherent case). Nat indexing encodes the first quadrant; SpectralSequence.AbutsTo is the finite decreasing subobject filtration of det-def-groth-ss. Site composition identifies the composite direct image, and punctual evaluation is global sections, as in the primary theorem docstring. The module theorem uses the same SheafOfModules category and module direct image as the recorded dependencies (the direct-image equality was checked by rfl on the server). Its HasInjectiveResolutions parameters are supplied by Scheme.Modules.isGrothendieckAbelian, explicitly installed in the server consumer probe. No new notion, theorem, extra mathematical assumption, or statement correction.
